summary: Lijiang suits atmospheric, slower travel built around old-town lanes, mountain views, cafe breaks, and soft day-to-night transitions.
transport_notes: Old town and nearby cultural areas are best grouped on the same day to avoid repeated in-and-out movement.
Mountain or farther scenic stops should be used selectively because they can easily dominate the day's pacing.
Evenings are strongest within or near the old town where walking and dining stay simple.

budget_notes.low: Focus on old-town walking, public viewpoints, and practical local dining with minimal transfers.
budget_notes.medium: Blend one old-town district, one mountain-view or cultural stop, and one atmospheric dining area each day.
budget_notes.high: Use slower boutique-style pacing, stronger scenic meals, and fewer high-friction route changes.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Lijiang should emphasize photogenic lanes, affordable cafe-and-snack rhythm, and flexible old-town movement.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should feel reflective, free-moving, and visually rich without needing complicated logistics.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should use old-town light, mountain silhouettes, and evening atmosphere as the emotional core.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should avoid overly steep or crowded routes and favor easier old-town or scenic edge experiences.
